title: The Role of Repos in Monetary Policy Implementation - Liberty Street Economics
gist: NY Fed staff explain how the Fed uses standing repos (SRP, a rate ceiling) and ON RRP (a rate floor) to manage liquidity and control overnight rates, noting repo usage clusters in reserve-scarcity episodes (Sept 2019, March 2020, late 2025 after ~2.5 years of QT). ON RRP peaked near $2.5T in early 2023 before draining as the balance sheet shrank; the piece also traces Fed repo design back to 1917.

insights.claim: The Fed's overnight standing repo operations (SRP), at a rate set by the FOMC, act as a ceiling on overnight rates by giving eligible counterparties funding that reduces their incentive to borrow at market rates above the SRP rate.
insights.speaker: Gara Afonso, Jun-Davinci Choi, Gonzalo Cisternas, and Will Riordan
insights.so_what: SRP rate is the effective cap on repo/funding rates; spikes above it signal operational frictions or stigma.
insights.quote: The SRP rate—set by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC)—provides a ceiling on overnight rates
insights.locator: How Does the Federal Reserve Use Repos and Reverse Repos?

insights.claim: The ON RRP rate sets a floor under overnight market rates by giving money market funds, banks and GSEs an overnight investment that reduces incentives to lend below that rate.
insights.speaker: Gara Afonso, Jun-Davinci Choi, Gonzalo Cisternas, and Will Riordan
insights.so_what: Front-end rates are bounded between ON RRP and SRP; money fund yields key off the floor.

insights.claim: Fed repos expand its balance sheet and add reserves only while outstanding; at maturity reserves are drained and the balance sheet shrinks.

insights.so_what: Repo-supplied liquidity is temporary, unlike asset purchases; heavy SRP use is a sign of reserve scarcity, not permanent easing.
